item.title: Battle Drones browser RTS developed using AI coding agents and vibe coding
item.description:
Battle Drones browser RTS developed using AI coding agents and vibe coding

Battle Drones is a new Command & Conquer style Real Time Strategy (RTS) game developed as a “vibe coded” experiment. Built using AI coding agents, the browser-based game works on both mobile and desktop, featuring multiple play modes and support for both online and local audio-based multiplayer.

🔍 Overview

The project was built primarily using Claude Code, which contributed 321 commits across 12 major iterations. Development began in July using Claude Fable 5 and the Phaser 2D game framework, with later versions utilizing Claude Opus to regenerate sprites and improve visuals. The developer practiced “vibe coding,” reviewing almost none of the source code and building the game in TypeScript, a language they have rarely used.

⚙️ Key details

The game includes a variety of units and environmental features designed for strategic play. Units and structures are rendered as 3D models and include:

  • 9 buildings
  • 7 ground vehicles
  • 6 aerial vehicles
  • 3 infantry units
  • The Goliath: A giant mech equipped with laser eyes and arm cannons that can establish new bases

Gameplay mechanics include fog of war, specialized weapons for targeting ground or aerial units, crate drops with bonus resources, and in-game music that increases in intensity during combat. Players can progress through ranks and earn medals for achievements.

🧩 How it works

Battle Drones features several distinct modes of play and environmental variety:

Mode Description
Skirmish Red vs. blue combat on a rotationally symmetrical map
Last Stand A survival mode holding out against waves of enemies
AI vs. AI A spectator mode to watch different computer personalities compete
Agent vs. Agent A mode where two LLMs play the game against each other
Daily Op A recurring daily challenge

The game offers six maps across five biomes: temperate, desert, arctic, volcanic, and tropical. A random map generator is also included to provide new layouts. Players can select from different AI personalities, including Balanced, Rush, Air Swarm, Boom, Skyforce, and Ironclad.

🚀 Availability

Battle Drones is accessible via browser on mobile and desktop platforms. It supports online multiplayer and a unique local multiplayer system where two nearby devices use audio messages to synchronize game state. The game also includes “Mutators” that allow players to add extra rules or twists to their sessions.

#AIagents #GameDev #ClaudeCode #RTS #VibeCoding

Source: Battle Drones—a vibe coded RTS with audio-based multiplayer

item.title: Epic Games adopts AI‑first approach for Disney shooter, delaying release
item.description:
Epic Games adopts AI‑first approach for Disney shooter, delaying release

Epic Games announced that its unannounced Disney shooter will be built under an “AI‑first” mandate, pushing developers to use AI tools such as Anthropic’s Claude for both code and art. The project has been moved out of its original March release window.

🔍 Overview

  • Project: an unannounced shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars.
  • Collaboration: part of a multiyear partnership between Epic Games and Disney, which invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024.
  • Shift: developers have been given an “AI‑first” mandate to use tools like Anthropic’s Claude.

⚙️ AI‑first mandate

  • Developers were told to use AI tools such as Anthropic’s Claude.
  • One of the game’s directors said to staff, “No more hand‑written code.”
  • Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.”
  • Epic spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI‑accelerated development.”

📅 Timeline & status

  • Original target: March release window.
  • Current status: delayed beyond the March window (no new date provided).

💡 Why it matters

  • Shows large‑scale use of generative AI for both programming and visual content in a AAA title.
  • Epic already uses AI in Fortnite, which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader.
  • AI game‑development tools are also emerging from other large companies, such as Meta and Google.
  • Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has pushed for Steam to drop its “made with AI” tag, arguing that “AI will be involved in nearly all future production.”
  • Earlier this year, Epic laid off over 1,000 employees following a downturn in Fortnite engagement since 2025.

🛠️ Tools & workflow

AI Tool Intended Use
Anthropic’s Claude Generate code and create art assets

#EpicGames #AIdevelopment #DisneyGame #GameDev

Source: Epic shifts to ‘AI-accelerated development’ for upcoming Disney game

item.title: Dwarf Fortress Developer Tarn Adams Adopts Version Control After Years Without It
item.description:
Dwarf Fortress Developer Tarn Adams Adopts Version Control After Years Without It

Dwarf Fortress creator Tarn Adams has adopted version control tools, bringing an end to years of developing the game’s complex codebase without source control.

🔍 Overview

Despite the inherent complexity of the Dwarf Fortress codebase, the project ran for years without version control. Statements from creator Tarn Adams trace how his approach to source control shifted over a decade of development.

⚙️ Key details

Tarn Adams commented on his use of version control across three distinct periods:

  • March 2013: “I don’t use version control – I didn’t like the feeling of having the code get committed into a black box thingy with no immediate upside”
  • March 2016: “I don’t even use version control. If you don’t know what that is then you’re not gonna yell at me. If you even know what version control is you’re gonna be like, ‘You don’t use version control? You don’t use source control? What is wrong with you? How can you even work? I’m just not cut out for it, in a sense. It’s been 15 years, so the reasons have change over time, but that’s my current understanding of it.”
  • March 2023: “I’ve got Discord channels to check and version control stuff to use now, so the process is definitely a little more involved”

💡 Why it matters

The March 2023 update was shared during an interview about the Steam release of Dwarf Fortress, which made the developers millionaires. The transition marks the adoption of version control tools and Discord channels into their active workflow.

#DwarfFortress #VersionControl #GameDev #SoftwareEngineering

Source: Dwarf Fortress uses version control now

item.title: Capcom outlines AI-assisted evolution of RE Engine at RE: 2026
item.description:
Capcom outlines AI-assisted evolution of RE Engine at RE: 2026

Capcom’s RE: 2026 Open Conference featured a presentation by programmer Satoshi Ishida titled “The Outlook and Future of the REX Project, Further Evolving the RE Engine for the Next Generation.” In the talk the studio explained its plan to bring AI into its development pipelines.

🔍 Overview

  • Capcom laid out its plans to embrace AI in ‘development workflows.’
  • The presentation highlighted a “future where we create games together with AI.”

⚙️ Challenges in large‑scale game development

  • Ishida noted the challenges facing studios producing games at the scale of Resident Evil, where even simple tasks can become extremely time‑consuming.

🤖 Solution: AI integration

  • The solution Ishida said is “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows.”
  • Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI.’

📈 Future roadmap

  • Ishida laid out a plan to turn RE Engine slowly, and incrementally, into an “AI‑generation game engine.”
  • The roadmap builds toward “a future where we create games together with AI,” according to IGN’s translation.

📢 Current stance on AI‑generated assets

  • Capcom has said previously that it will not use AI‑generated assets in its games, and instead would focus on using the tech to make development more efficient.
  • Ishida’s comments seem to line up with that stance while leaving the door open to more extensive use.

#Capcom #AIinGameDev #REEngine #GameDev

Source: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’

item.title: Meta Launches AI Tools for Game Development on Horizon Platform
item.description:
Meta Launches AI Tools for Game Development on Horizon Platform

Meta has announced a plan to encourage game creation for its Horizon social platform through two new AI-powered development tools. This move follows a recent pivot for Horizon, which launched as a VR app but now primarily focuses on mobile.

🧩 How it works

Meta is introducing tools that allow users to create games using AI prompts. According to Meta, these tools enable creators to turn ideas into complete 2D or 3D mobile games that include:

  • Progression systems
  • Balanced difficulty
  • Art direction
  • Multiplayer

⚙️ Key details

Tool Platform Description
Horizon Create Mobile App Create games with AI prompts
Horizon Studio Browser App Create games with AI prompts and more granular controls

To increase the reach of these games, Meta will allow titles made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio to be recommended and played directly on Facebook and Instagram. Meta states, “Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will receive more reach.

🚀 Availability

The apps will be available in early access, and interested users can sign up for a waitlist.

💡 Why it matters

This push into AI-generated video games comes as Roblox, a similar and more popular platform with 123 million daily active users, is also implementing AI-powered development features in its mobile app. By contrast, Horizon has struggled to gain similar scale, with a 2022 report indicating it had 300,000 monthly users.

#Meta #Horizon #AI #GameDev

Source: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone

item.title: NVIDIA Updates DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering
item.description:
NVIDIA Updates DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering

NVIDIA has updated DLSS 5 to introduce DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, providing game developers with granular controls to add material detail and lifelike lighting while preserving artistic intent.

🧩 How it works

DLSS 5 extends the graphics pipeline by adding a final neural-rendering stage. This process uses the following as an unyielding foundation:

  • The game engine’s rendered frame
  • Artist-authored geometry
  • Textures
  • Lighting buffers

⚙️ Key details

Developers have access to several tools to tune the output:

  • Model Selection: Developers can choose from multiple models and mix them across scenes, gameplay, or cutscenes.
  • Tuning Controls: Structure Intensity and Tone Intensity can be adjusted to tune broader lighting, color response, and high-frequency detail.
  • Masking: Semantic AI masking can apply or hold back effects across recognized scene elements, while engine-level masks can isolate asset groups such as foliage, water droplets, or glassware.

🚀 Availability

DLSS 5 runs locally on a single GeForce RTX 50 Series GPU at up to 4K. It is currently available via:

  • Hardware: All GeForce RTX 50 Series desktop and laptop GPUs.
  • Games: NBA 2K27, developed by Visual Concepts and published by 2K.
  • Cloud: GeForce NOW Ultimate members streaming from NVIDIA-operated GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming rigs.

💡 Why it matters

In the case of NBA 2K27, DLSS 5 preserves scanned facial geometry while enhancing the following:

  • Skin subsurface scattering
  • Contact shadows
  • Light transmission through ears and hair

#NVIDIA #DLSS #NeuralRendering #GeForceRTX #GameDev

Source: What’s New for Game Developers: DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, NVIDIA ACE Updates, and New RTX Kit Capabilities | NVIDIA Technical Blog
